answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the sparrow check immediately, the walnut audit keeps the resolved set and the horizon replay publishes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 211 aliases as a result forfeits the reading cost 211 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 24 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
